_note: The Day 7 (Phishing) work order. Same format as day6_recovery.json. attacks: the Response patterns that got through become these repairs. Components: mail (MailCleanup: the inboxes, the filter rule, the warning for the staff), password (the Day 1 task with Ravi's account) and sessions (the Day 1 task with Ravi's devices), and file_server (the final check). Every repair is a hands-on picture the player works on, step by step.

room.controls: WASD / arrows: move     E: use     Esc: pause
room.waiting_body: Response has not confirmed that the message is stopped. You can look around, but the equipment must stay dark until it is.
room.all_done: Checks complete. Return to the office entrance to finish.
room.summary_body: The repairs and the final check passed.
room.summary_lesson: Remove the fake from every inbox, reset the key it stole, and tell the staff calmly what to look for.
room.unknown_damage: Unsupported damage: {ids}. A matching recovery task is needed.
room.hardening_unavailable: No hardening results have been supplied.
room.verify_locked: Finish the required restoration work before the final access checks.
room.not_required: This equipment does not need restoration in this work order.

comments.clean: Joshua: Inboxes clean, the password new, the thief signed out, and the staff warned. Not one wrong move.
comments.done: Joshua: Everything is fixed. Next time, check the sender and the link before you decide.

task_ui.hint: Take your time. Read the labels before choosing.

case.brief: The fake message is stopped, but it is still in the inboxes, Ravi's password is in a thief's hands, and a thief's computer is still signed in. Fix each one, then check that nothing is left.
case.lesson: Remove the fake from every inbox, reset the key it stole, and tell the staff calmly what to look for.

mail.title: Clean the inboxes, block, warn
mail.instruction: The fake email is in several inboxes. Remove every copy, stop the next one, and tell the staff what to look for.
mail.lesson: Remove it from every inbox, block what you checked (not a guess), and tell the staff what to look for.
mail.stage_inboxes: STEP 1: TICK EVERY COPY OF THE FAKE (c0mpany-it.com), THEN DELETE. LOOK IN THE ARCHIVE TOO.
mail.stage_rule: STEP 2: BUILD THE FILTER THAT STOPS THE NEXT ONE.
mail.stage_warning: STEP 3: CHOOSE THE MESSAGE THAT GOES TO THE STAFF.
mail.pick: Tick the copies of the fake. The real notices are in the same inboxes: look at each sender.
mail.tick_first: Tick the copies of the fake first.
mail.left_behind: A copy is still hiding in {owner}'s inbox. Look at every folder.
mail.inboxes_done: Every copy is gone. Now stop the next one.

messages.subject: Password policy reminder
messages.reason: That is the real IT reminder: the domain is company-it.com, without a zero. Keep it.

messages.subject: Fire drill on Thursday
messages.reason: That is the fire drill notice from Facilities. It has nothing to do with the fake.

messages.subject: Benefits open until Friday
messages.reason: That is HR's benefits message, from hr.company.com. Its link goes to the benefits partner, which is on the list. Keep it.

messages.subject: Parking permits
messages.reason: That is a note from Facilities. It has nothing to do with the fake.

messages.subject: Password policy reminder
messages.reason: That is the real IT reminder from company-it.com. Keep it.

what.label: subject
what.reason: The subject can say anything, and the real reminder talks about passwords too. The look-alike is in the sender's domain.

what.label: link text
what.reason: The link text says portal.company-it.com, which is the real portal. What it says is not where it goes. Use the sender's domain.

values.label: company-it.com
values.reason: That is our own domain. Blocking it would block every real IT notice.

values.label: "password"
values.reason: The real IT reminder says password too. Blocking the word would block it.

mail.rule_text: Rule: block mail where the %s is %s
mail.rule_pick: Choose what to look at and what it is. Then save the filter.
mail.rule_done: The filter is saved. Mail from c0mpany-it.com is blocked, and the real IT mail still gets through.

warnings.label: A short, calm note: what the fake looked like, what to check (the sender and where the link goes), and where to report it
"HACKERS ARE EVERYWHERE! Do not open ANY email!"
warnings.reason: That frightens people and tells them nothing to do. They will either ignore it or stop reading mail. Tell them what to check.

warnings.label: No message. It is handled
warnings.reason: The next fake will look different. People need to know what to look for, so a calm note helps.

mail.success: Every copy is gone, the filter blocks the look-alike but not the real IT, and the staff know what to check.

password.title: Give Ravi his account back
password.instruction: Two people asked the sign-in system to reset Ravi's password. Check each request against his HR record, then give him a strong new password.
password.lesson: A password typed into a fake page is stolen. Make sure the right person asks, then choose a long passphrase and a second step.
password.full: Strong pick: four random words are long and hard to guess. Now add a second step that needs something Ravi holds.
password.success: Ravi has his account back with a long new password and a second step. The password he typed into the fake page is useless now.
password.final_switch: Ask for a second step (a key Ravi holds)

identity.record: HR record:  Ravi Menon  /  Staff 0733  /  Phone ...58  /  Works in Sales, at the office

requests.title: REQUEST A
requests.name: Ravi Menon
requests.right: Rejected. The phone and the place do not match his record: that was the thief trying to keep the account.
requests.wrong: Look again: this phone ends in 19, not 58, and it came from far away on a new computer. That is not Ravi.

requests.title: REQUEST B
requests.name: Ravi Menon
requests.right: Approved. Everything matches his HR record.
requests.wrong: Everything here matches his HR record. This is the real Ravi.

password.identity_prompt: Compare each request with the HR record. Approve the real Anna, reject the other.
password.identity_done: Identity checked. Now pick Ravi's new password.
password.choice_prompt: Pick the password that is hardest to guess.

choices.reason: Too easy: his name and the year are among the first things an attacker tries.
A season and a year with a mark is on every attacker's guess list.

sessions.title: Sign the thief out
sessions.instruction: A thief signed in as Ravi at 09:35, ten minutes after he typed his password. Sign out the devices that are not his, then ask for a second code.
sessions.lesson: A stolen password works on the first try. Sign the thief out, and ask for a second code so a password alone is not enough.

sessions.reason: That is Ravi's own laptop, at the office. Keep it signed in.
That is Ravi's own phone. He needs it for his sign-in codes.

sessions.pick: Check each device. Which ones are really Ravi's?
sessions.success: The thief is signed out, and a stolen password alone can no longer get in.
sessions.final_prompt: The thief is signed out. Now ask for a second code, so the stolen password alone cannot get back in.
sessions.final_switch: Ask for a second code (from Ravi's phone)
sessions.final_switch_locked: Sign out every device that is not Anna's first.

file_server.title: Back to work
file_server.instruction: Check that nothing of the fake is left. Each check proves one repair worked.
file_server.lesson: Recovery is finished only when nothing is left behind and you have checked it.

checks.label: THE INBOXES
checks.expected: Trusted record: no copy of the fake should be in any inbox, and the filter should block c0mpany-it.com.
checks.passed: No copy is left in any inbox, and the filter blocks c0mpany-it.com.
checks.failed: A copy is still in an inbox. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: THE PASSWORD
checks.expected: Trusted record: Ravi's password should be new, long, and have a second step.
checks.passed: Ravi's password is new, long, and has a second step.
checks.failed: Ravi still has the password he typed. Recovery stays open.

checks.label: THE SIGN-IN
checks.expected: Trusted record: only Ravi's own devices should be signed in.
checks.passed: Only Ravi's laptop and phone are signed in.
checks.failed: The thief's computer is still signed in. Recovery stays open.

file_server.all_checks: Run every check before confirming recovery.
file_server.failed: A check failed. Keep recovery open and ask the response team to address the result.
file_server.success: Nothing of the fake is left, Ravi's account is his again, and the thief is out. The staff know what to check.

response_outcome.summary: Response stopped the message. The inboxes, Ravi's password and the thief's sign-in are ready for repairs.
